turns.zh: 它已经演变了很多。大约 6 个月或一年前，团队规模小得多时，情况非常不同。比如团队今年增长了 4 倍——我想说在 9、10 个月内——所以这是一个进行中的工作，我的演变。我一周中最关心的核心结构是我喜欢在周五晚上看工程演示。我不知道，这让我——我喜欢看正在构建什么、已经构建了什么或已经交付了什么，将其与我真的关心的某些客户价值联系起来。我经常在周一与我的领导团队共度时光。主要是因为每个周末对我来说都是一个新的痴迷或旅程。就像周一到周五，我认为你处于日常运营中。每个周末你上升一步，想出我们缺少什么？我应该对什么保持偏执？我们应该去创建一个新的业务领域吗？我需要去雇佣一个有特殊技能的人吗？我需要以不同的方式思考客户或市场吗？所以每个周末你最终——至少我通常的目标是从三个正在冒泡的痴迷中选择一个，并尝试在周一早上得出结论，要么这个痴迷不是我应该采取行动的——一半的时候这是正确答案——要么这个痴迷似乎值得追求，我会把一些事情交给某人去将其提升到下一个层次。然后我会在某个地方跟进它，对吧？所以对我来说，这就是我的循环，有点围绕周末和一周的其他时间。我们有一个公司的事情，我们在一个办公室面对面办公。每个人都在同一个办公室，产品和工程在帕洛阿尔托的周一、周三和周五。住在旧金山的人在周二和周四去我们的旧金山办公室，对吧？所以现在我与人的内部时间，我尽量把周一、周三、周五尽可能多地保留给那个。外部的事情尽可能在周二和周四做。所以结果就形成了一些自然的节奏，对吧？嗯，一般来说我不喜欢安排——几乎没有安排的一对一会议。

turns.en: One-on-ones.
turns.zh: 一对一会议。

turns.en: No one-on-ones with anybody. We're pretty flat. Um no one-on-ones. We don't have people that need too many one-on-ones, but it's always one-on-ones, right? Like I'm always in the office and anyone walks up and you can have a three-minute conversation about anything. And I mostly process things by—as I'm walking in the office, I see a face and then I'm reminded of like oh there was something that was brewing. Let me go figure this out with this person.
turns.zh: 和任何人都没有一对一会议。我们相当扁平。嗯，没有一对一会议。我们没有需要太多一对一会议的人，但它总是随时的面对面交流，对吧？比如我总是在办公室，任何人走过来，你都可以就任何事情进行三分钟的对话。我主要处理事情的方式是——当我在办公室走动时，我看到一张脸，然后我想起哦，有些事情正在酝酿。让我去和这个人弄清楚。

turns.en: How much of your time are you spending on recruiting now?
turns.zh: 你现在花多少时间在招聘上？

turns.en: Recruiting is always a steady amount of time, but then there are periods of intense activity.
turns.zh: 招聘总是稳定的时间量，但也会有密集活动的时期。

turns.en: But is it like 25% or—
turns.zh: 但是像 25% 还是——

turns.en: In aggregate, yeah. But I think there are some weeks which will be lower, but certain weeks where there is like one job. Right? Like I think we've recently—I think now we in the spring got our amazing head of sales, Graham. Most recently we got our head of marketing Elaine. Right around then we got head of finance, Adil. Really amazing people, but each of these are consequential hires. So each of these you obsess about a lot of heartburn about like is this the right person? Is this the right thing? A lot of time with the person, but also a lot of time making sure you know what you want. Are you going to set them up the right way? So recruiting isn't just about the interview, right? Like that is I think like a sliver. Real mental energy and time goes into all the other things and half of it is done after they show up.
turns.zh: 总的来说，是的。但我认为有些周会更低，但某些周会有像一个职位。对吧？就像我认为我们最近——我想现在我们在春天得到了我们出色的销售主管 Graham。最近我们得到了营销主管 Elaine。大约那时我们得到了财务主管 Adil。非常出色的人，但每一个都是重要的招聘。所以每一个你都会痴迷，很多焦虑，比如这是对的人吗？这是对的事情吗？花很多时间和这个人在一起，但也花很多时间确保你知道你想要什么。你会以正确的方式设置他们吗？所以招聘不仅仅是面试，对吧？就像我认为那只是一小部分。真正的脑力和时间花在所有其他事情上，其中一半是在他们出现之后完成的。

turns.en: You talked about hiring for two types of alpha when we were chatting before this. So can you double click on that? Like what's your philosophy on what you look for?
turns.zh: 在我们之前聊天时，你谈到了招聘两种类型的 alpha。你能详细说说吗？比如你寻找什么的哲学是什么？

turns.en: Yeah, so this is like goes back to Twitter days, at least my biases is I always thought of—listen, like when you are the person that wants to get hired to do jobs that you're not entirely deserving of. And if you decide that for yourself, that is the best way to maximize your career, your prospects, your impact, whatever you might want to do it.
turns.zh: 是的，所以这就像回到 Twitter 时代，至少我的偏见是我总是想到——听着，就像当你是一个想要被雇佣去做你并不完全配得上的工作的人。如果你为自己决定这一点，那是最大化你的职业、你的前景、你的影响力的最佳方式，无论你可能想做什么。

transcript.sec: Hiring for Potential and Building Teams

turns.en: Then you have to simultaneously believe that you only want to be able to hire those people, right? Like if there is someone, I have to figure out the best people I believe will want to be hired for things that are a challenge. If they have been there, done that, do they want to do that thing again? Or do they want a new challenge which will push them on a journey to learn and grow and do something that will give you the satisfaction saying like, oh going into this, I didn't know that I could do this or we could do this. Doesn't it feel great when you do it?
turns.zh: 那么你必须同时相信，你只想能够雇佣那些人，对吧？比如如果有一个人，我必须找出我认为最优秀的人，他们愿意被雇佣来做有挑战性的事情。如果他们曾经做过、有经验，他们还想再做一次吗？还是他们想要一个新的挑战，推动他们踏上学习和成长的旅程，去做一些能给你带来满足感的事情，让你说：哦，进入这个领域时，我不知道我能做到这个，或者我们能一起做到这个。当你做到时，感觉不是很好吗？

turns.en: So you look for more potential rather than they've done the job.
turns.zh: 所以你更看重潜力，而不是他们做过这份工作。

turns.en: Correct. So that is what you mean by alpha, right? Like you have to make bets on people which feel like bets. And but now if you're in the business of hiring a lot of people where you're just making bets, right? You are mostly hiring some form of outliers. Now you also have to pull the team together, a team of outliers together, right? And so now you have to ask the question, who are the people who are exceptional at building these unique, weird teams where you have bet on potential? And there I at least find that I want to see on that dimension evidence that they have done that. They have worked with teams of exceptional outlier people who aren't of the type of been there, done that and created an environment where they can all do their best work and grow and learn which is not like default like management best practices, but like creating sort of the special teams that create this special moments, right? So you hire people who've done that, but then you challenge them by my principle on a different dimension, which they might not have encountered, right? So that sort of how you build teams, but like I think it's like a it's fundamentally a slightly non-scalable way of thinking about team building where you're trying to take bespoke individuals and creating something out of that instead of saying like, oh, I have this thing, I'm going to cut it up, divide up roles and responsibilities. So it requires a different kind of agility in leaders or managers, different kind of agility and plasticity among the people who show up into this. But I think that's what the early special teams are built off.

You can't have this rapid change with no potential downside risk, right? But you're already seeing people feel accountable enough to do that. Now you can say they should do more and you can have a reasonable disagreement, right?
turns.zh: 是的，不，我认为它们会，对吧？例如，网络风险正在出现。你已经在没有法律的情况下看到。构建这些模型的人首先尝试以任何方式。你可以怀疑他们的意图以及他们是否纯粹。但我认为他们正在努力让世界为网络竞赛做好准备。他们试图让人们找到问题并在它们变得广泛可利用之前解决它们。他们可能牺牲自己的产品体验和用例来最小化风险，他们试图在各个维度上做出风险回报的判断，这对我来说就是应该的方式，对吧？你不能有这种快速变化而没有潜在的下行风险，对吧？但你已经看到人们感到足够负责任去做这件事。现在你可以说他们应该做更多，你可以有合理的分歧，对吧？

turns.en: Please steal man that just for the debate, right? Uh bad technologies have existed forever. All technology can be used for good and bad. So uh guns are regulated, but even driving is regulated, right? Like you have to have a license, you can't be drunk and driving. So why shouldn't there be more regulation here?
turns.zh: 请为辩论公正地阐述对方观点，对吧？呃，坏技术一直存在。所有技术都可以用于善与恶。所以呃，枪支受到监管，但甚至驾驶也受到监管，对吧？就像你必须要有驾照，你不能酒后驾车。那么为什么这里不应该有更多监管呢？

turns.en: I'm I'm not saying there shouldn't be. I am saying that a lot of regulation has intended effects and unintended effects. And at least my lived experience is there exists a reasonable class of regulations especially around technology that tend to have negative and unintended effects. So now the burden I'm not saying no to all regulation. I am saying the burden of proof is on the specific regulatory framework we use and how we make sure that it is it is very likely to have the desired effects and not the undesirable risks. To me that is the burden of proof and the proposals that you see out and about to me don't meet that burden. That's what I'm saying.
turns.zh: 我我并不是说不应该有监管。我是说很多监管有预期效果和意外效果。至少我的亲身经历是，存在一类合理的监管，尤其是围绕技术的监管，往往会产生负面和意外效果。所以现在举证责任，我不是说反对所有监管。我是说举证责任在于我们使用的具体监管框架，以及我们如何确保它很可能产生预期效果而不是不良风险。对我来说这就是举证责任，而你所看到的那些提案对我来说没有达到这个举证责任。这就是我要说的。

turns.en: What do you think about the social upheaval that might be coming from a jobs perspective? I know it's a speculative question but where where is your heart and mind right now in five years, 10 years? Do you believe software engineering jobs go away or do they just evolve? Is there social upheaval coming or people just need to upgrade their skill sets or change their skill sets?
turns.zh: 你如何看待可能从就业角度出现的社会动荡？我知道这是一个推测性问题，但你现在的心和头脑在五年、十年后在哪里？你认为软件工程工作会消失还是只是演变？社会动荡会到来，还是人们只需要升级技能或改变技能？

turns.en: I think if this change was happening slowly I would have taken a I'm a tech optimist and I'm a optimist in our ability as people in society to evolve. That is my baseline point of view. In this moment the rate of change and the potential rate of change feels high enough that I don't feel the optimist conviction to sit here and tell you that like oh there is like society will evolve around this technology and everything will be great. Like I don't feel that way. I think the delta between the AI diffusion is like very uneven right now. Like we kind of here in San Francisco live in like a weird bubble where you're surrounded by people who live in the bubble and kind of believe more in AI and when you pop out of the bubble the world is different. Then you go even further the world is very different. So I don't know I feel the rate of change is high enough that there is a I think in the long arc society will evolve but along the way there are likely to be hard periods and yeah, so I worry about that. I I don't have meaningful constructive solutions
turns.zh: 我认为如果这种变化发生得缓慢，我会采取，我是一个技术乐观主义者，我对我们作为人和社会进化的能力持乐观态度。这是我的基线观点。此时此刻，变化的速度和潜在的变化速度感觉足够高，以至于我没有乐观的信念坐在这里告诉你，哦，社会将围绕这项技术进化，一切都会很好。我没有那种感觉。我认为目前 AI 扩散的差距非常不均匀。就像我们在旧金山生活在一个奇怪的泡沫中，你周围都是生活在泡沫中的人，他们更相信 AI，当你跳出泡沫，世界是不同的。然后你走得更远，世界非常不同。所以我不知道，我觉得变化的速度足够高，我认为从长远来看社会会进化，但沿途可能会有艰难时期，是的，所以我担心这个。我没有有意义的建设性解决方案

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: other than the piece of advice that I would give myself which is adapt as fast as humanly possible to the world around you. So try to assume that there is going to be this large continued rate of change and try really hard to adapt alongside it and bring the people around you and help others adapt to.
turns.zh: 除了我会给自己的建议，那就是尽可能快地适应周围的世界。所以试着假设会有这种巨大的持续变化率，并努力与之一起适应，并带动你周围的人，帮助他人适应。

turns.en: Do you believe the number of software jobs in five to 10 years will be dramatically less?
turns.zh: 你认为五到十年后软件工作的数量会大幅减少吗？

turns.en: I don't know how to define a software job in five to 10 years. I think the jobs will look different. I also think like I'm in the extreme positive sum game. So I think there will be way more value creation as a result of what you might define. The TAM will be much larger. That I believe. The economy around this will be much larger.
turns.zh: 我不知道如何定义五到十年后的软件工作。我认为工作会看起来不同。我也认为我处于极端正和游戏中。所以我认为由于你可能定义的东西，会有更多的价值创造。TAM 会大得多。我相信这一点。围绕这个的经济会大得多。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Now how many people will do that? I don't really know. Right? So in aggregate the economy around this will be much much much larger. Now the question is will it take way more people to support that large economy? Will it take the same number of people? Will it be like a regular growth like we've seen over many decades? Will be shrinkage? Like I honestly don't have a framework to know.
turns.zh: 现在有多少人会做这个？我真的不知道。对吧？所以总的来说，围绕这个的经济会大得多得多。现在的问题是，支持那个大经济需要更多的人吗？需要相同数量的人吗？会像我们几十年来看到的常规增长吗？会收缩吗？老实说我没有框架知道。

turns.en: How are you guiding your own kids for the skills that will be relevant for them in years to come, right? For you the curiosity, the math skills really panned out well.
turns.zh: 你如何引导自己的孩子培养未来几年相关的技能？对你来说，好奇心、数学技能真的很有成效。

turns.en: Yeah, but I think
turns.zh: 是的，但我认为

turns.en: those listen, it's like not hard to believe that. You will need hard work in the future. You will need curiosity in the future. You will need to communicate with the world and other people and models. So those baseline things are the same. I think you at least I feel that as a parent you have a role to play in those. You have a role to play in creating the environment and their peer group. But I don't think it's up to me to really decide like what they pursue or what catches their fancy at what age, right? And I think like I have evolved from being happy go lucky to math to physics to computer science to software engineering to leadership to founders. Like it's like these are arcs various times different things. Kids will evolve, right? Like I think middle school you'll have different interests. In high school it could evolve. Over time it could evolve. Who knows what college you'll be by the time that they're there. But if they be curious, I want to make it so. Should they enjoy sport and athletics? Yes. Should they enjoy teamwork in some of those pursuits? Yes. Should they work hard? Yes. Should they enjoy music? I hope so or art or something else. Um so these are like not complicated things and these are essentially all you as a parent get to play around with anyways, right? But I do think one thing I really feel great like is my kids appear to be hard working. They probably get that from my wife.
turns.zh: 听着，这并不难相信。未来你需要努力工作。未来你需要好奇心。你需要与世界、他人和模型沟通。所以这些基本的东西是一样的。我认为你，至少我觉得作为父母，你在这些方面有角色要扮演。你在创造环境和他们的同伴群体方面有角色要扮演。但我不认为是我来决定他们追求什么或在什么年龄什么吸引他们，对吧？我认为我从快乐随性到数学到物理到计算机科学到软件工程到领导力到创始人。就像这些是不同时期的弧线。孩子会进化，对吧？我认为初中你会有不同的兴趣。高中可能会进化。随着时间的推移可能会进化。谁知道他们上大学时会怎样。但如果他们好奇，我想使之如此。他们应该享受运动和体育吗？是的。他们应该在那些追求中享受团队合作吗？是的。他们应该努力工作吗？是的。他们应该享受音乐吗？我希望如此，或者艺术或其他什么。嗯，所以这些并不复杂，这些基本上都是你作为父母无论如何都可以玩的，对吧？但我确实认为我真正感觉很好的一件事是我的孩子似乎很努力。他们可能从我的妻子那里得到这个。

turns.en: So last question for you. A young person watching this wants your life, wants the life that you've built.
turns.zh: 所以最后一个问题。一个观看此节目的年轻人想要你的生活，想要你建立的生活。

turns.en: What would you tell them that this journey actually requires?
turns.zh: 你会告诉他们，这段旅程实际上需要什么？

turns.en: Hard work, a great peer group, getting lucky with a lot of things including family, choosing the right spouse, and only working and getting lucky enough to only get to work on things that you really enjoy. Right? That's not a privilege you can take for granted, but I've gotten a bunch of the ingredients right and made a few good decisions which were consequential. That's what it takes.
turns.zh: 努力，一个优秀的同行圈子，在很多事情上运气好，包括家庭，选对伴侣，以及努力并且运气足够好，只去做你真正享受的事情。对吧？这不是你可以理所当然享有的特权，但我把很多要素都凑对了，也做了几个影响重大的好决定。这就是所需要的。

turns.en: Parag, this is amazing. Thank you so much for coming on.
turns.zh: Parag，这太精彩了。非常感谢你来参加。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好的。
